why.say:
• The only gap explanation that holds up is John Doe's own, in his words, backed by documents
• Compare "Was it because you had no car?" with "What, if anything, made it hard to get seen sooner?"
• The job: draw it out and write it down exactly; never explain, defend or judge it
• Red flag: "Was it because you had no car?" A leading question buys a yes, not information; ask it open

theory.say:
• Gap interview roadmap: plan the questions, never the answers expected
• Open on the record: date, who is on, role, his consent to record, privacy
• Ask open, follow his words, ask for the paper, read it back, open a dated task per document
• Coordinate, don't commingle: keep the medical and legal tracks separate in notes
• Write facts, never conclusions; an opinion in a note is something the defense can use

frame.say:
• A-C-T: the three-step plan when care goes wrong: Assess, Coordinate, Track
• Assess: medical danger, like a fever or loose hardware, goes to the doctor today; legal danger goes to Atty. Thorne
• A gap in treatment is a legal danger
• Coordinate: call the provider's office and clear the barrier the client names: rides, scheduling, a referral
• Track: log the flag and every fix the same day, then ask again: is the plan working?

rules.say:
• Investigate, don't advocate: read the EMS report, the 02/20/2026 urgent-care history and the timeline; plan questions only
• Funnel: broad open questions, then follow-ups on his words, yes-or-no last to pin a date or document
• Never lead or judge; never offer the usual reasons, like rides, co-pays or work schedules
• Record only with spoken consent; a Keystone Recorded Statement request is politely declined and sent to the firm
• Confirm the 03/05/2026 Dr. Reyes consult and his rides after 03/19/2026; "the gap won't matter" is legal advice

model.say:
• Green column, ask it open; red column, never like this; each open question sits beside the leading version it replaces
• Last red row, tagged UPL (unauthorized practice of law): the soothing line, an opinion on his case
• Funnel below: open first, follow his words, then pin dates and documents; recorded, consent on the record
• Same fact asked two ways gives two different cases

steps.say:
• Records show the 14-day gap; read the EMS report, urgent-care history and treatment timeline in the CMS
• Save the questions-only plan in Case Notes before the call; no question names a reason
• Call Simulator, AI John Doe: state the date, who is on, that it's recorded; get consent, confirm privacy
• Privilege, the protection on client and firm talk, needs privacy, not an audience
• Asked what the gap does to his case: no opinion; log it, route to Atty. Thorne through Tasks same day

dodont.say:
• Do: ask open, follow his words, close last; read his story back so he can correct it
• Do: prevent the next gap now; cheaper than explaining a second one in the demand
• Weak: "Was it because you had no car?" Strong: hears the car, soreness, cost worry, numbness from 02/18
• Don't: name the expected reason, blame him for the gap, or reassure or alarm him; both are case opinions
dodont.ask: What separates saying consistent care matters from saying what this gap does to his case?

why.say:
• Clients go quiet for ordinary reasons: pain, overwhelm, a changed phone
• When a client goes silent, the case and its deadlines keep running
• No Contact Protocol: the step-by-step plan when a client stops answering
• Three jobs: track the silence officially, prove the firm tried, protect the firm if questioned later
• Red flag: two voicemails, 02/11 and 02/13, left and never logged; an unlogged attempt didn't happen
• Log every attempt with the date, the time, the channel and what came of it

theory.say:
• Look inside the file first: case status, deadlines, last contact
• Then the ladder: two calls, email and text, emergency contact, certified letter (mail with proof of delivery)
• Then tell Atty. Thorne what the silence puts at risk
• Due diligence: written proof of a real, reasonable effort; approved channels: the contact ways agreed at intake
• Emergency contact on this file: Margaret Doe, his mother

frame.say:
• Silence usually starts with a bottleneck: a spot where the work slows or gets stuck
• Missing information like a wrong number, slow follow-up, a Conflict Check stuck in backlog
• Intake forms with wrong dates or missing signatures, facts needing attorney review, gaps between departments
• Check the firm's own bottlenecks before blaming the client; a gap on the firm's side weakens the demand

rules.say:
• Step 1, internal review: status, live deadlines, last contact date, before dialling
• Step 2, the ladder: at least two calls, then email and text, emergency contact, certified mail or formal letter
• Climb by channel, not by volume; nine calls to one number is not trying everything
• Log each attempt with date, time, channel and outcome, plus a follow-up reminder
• Step 3: tell Atty. Thorne; tell the client what is needed and by when, never that the case is dropped

model.say:
• Six stations: internal review, contact attempts, team notification in colour; Steps 4 to 6 greyed for the next lesson
• Station two opens into the ladder: phone, email and text, emergency contact, certified mail
• Each rung is wider: it reaches further and costs more; don't skip rungs or stay on one
• Red card: the statute of limitations, the legal deadline to file suit, keeps running throughout

steps.say:

dodont.say:

• Do: make answering easy; as a Northgate shift lead he can't take calls on the floor, so text or upload link

theory.say:
• Final Warning Letter: the last written notice and last cheap step before paying to find the client or the attorney ending the case
• Two jobs: specific enough that the client answers, documented enough to back up what comes next
• Sent two ways: certified mail proves delivery; email is what people read
• Three-criteria gate: ladder done, letter sent, letter's deadline passed; all three before acting, the cheap letter before the expensive search
• Skip-trace: a paid search for a current address and phone; it costs money, so the attorney approves
• Withdrawal: the firm stops representing the client; only the attorney decides, under firm and court rules

frame.say:
• Step 4, Final Warning Letter: earlier attempts listed, 7 to 14 days to respond, warning the firm may withdraw
• Step 5, no answer: the attorney decides on a Notice or Motion to Withdraw, telling the court the firm is leaving
• Step 6: close the file "No response, withdrew per protocol," keeping every proof
• The Case Manager drives the letter and builds the record behind Steps 5 and 6

rules.say:
• Step 4 goes by certified mail and email, both: attempts listed, 7 to 14 day deadline, possible withdrawal
• Confirm the current address first; a letter to a stale address proves nothing
• Skip-trace only with all three conditions met and counsel's approval, full log attached
• Real dates, like "Called 02/10, voicemail 02/13," not "tried several times"
• Withdrawal may be called possible; never judge the claim or announce the case is over

model.say:
• Left: the letter on letterhead, four required parts: attempts listed, 7 to 14 day deadline, withdrawal possible, how to respond
• Above it: certified mail AND email, not either
• Right: the Step 5 fork: response by the deadline? Yes, the file picks back up
• No: a gate of three chips, ladder done, letter sent, deadline passed, before skip-trace and the attorney's decision

dodont.say:

• Don't: start a skip-trace on one condition alone, or announce withdrawal in a letter the attorney never approved
• Weak: a vague please-call note; strong: every attempt by date, a clear deadline, withdrawal possible
• The Case Manager builds the record; only the attorney ends representation
• Red flag: a draft that says the firm is withdrawing or "you will lose your case"; strike it, that decision is Atty. Thorne's alone
• The draft goes to Atty. Thorne before it goes anywhere
dodont.ask: Who decides that representation is ending, and who tells the client?

map.say:
• Check in on visits, pain, function and barriers: anything stopping him getting to care
• Name the variance: clinical (medical), psychosocial (life or mood), or systemic (the system stuck)
• Assess: medical danger to the provider, legal danger to Atty. Thorne; Coordinate: clarify and remove the barrier
• Track: every fix in a GIRP note, Goal, Intervention, Response, Plan; facts only

theory.say:
• On an LOP nobody denies visits in real time; Keystone challenges the care at the demand
• Week-6 mark, 04/07/2026, six weeks after first therapy on 02/24/2026: doctors check therapy is working; John missed it
• Care off the Standard Treatment Map triggers denials and IMEs, exams by the insurer's doctor
• Acute, days 1 to 14: ER, imaging, first therapy, proving the crash caused the injury; sub-acute, weeks 2 to 8: active therapy, specialists, measured gains
• Restorative, weeks 9 to 24: injections, work hardening; then maintenance; MMI, Maximum Medical Improvement, opens pre-demand
• You are the only real-time check: off the map, act that day, ask and record why, not "missed visits"

theory2.say:
• A-C-T: the immediate move for any red flag; its record gives Atty. Thorne the why
• "Reasonable and necessary": the insurer's test; normal care for this crash, with measurable gain
• SMART goals: specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound, like the week-6 measures
• Stakeholder triad: clinical, legal and money loops, the Case Manager as switchboard; one broken loop stalls a case

frame.say:
• Acute, days 1 to 14: ER, MRI or CT, brace, rest and ice, first therapy; establish causation and PIP
• Sub-acute, weeks 2 to 8: therapy two or three times weekly; week 6 looks for 20 to 30 percent better motion
• Restorative, weeks 9 to 24: work hardening, injections, emotional adjustment, return-to-work barriers
• Maintenance after week 24: home exercise, watch for MMI, which opens the pre-demand audit
• Adjusters lay the records over this map; each mismatch lowers the offer

rules.say:
• Monitor outcomes, not attendance: visits, pain, limits at work and home, inside and outside barriers
• 04/08/2026 is day 61, week 9; the week-6 mark was 04/07/2026, 02/24/2026 plus 42 days
• Name the variance, run A-C-T for every red flag, adjust the plan first; coordinate care, never direct it; never say missed visits cut his claim
• Climb one documented rung at a time: clinical, administrative, legal; write every intervention as a GIRP note
• Red flag: on A-C-T, the plan runs on unchanged through a crisis, or somebody puts a label on John
• Document his distress in his own words, never diagnose, and adjust the plan with his consent

model.say:

• Track curves back into the ring: A-C-T closes back into monitoring
• Corner: the treatment map, marker on restorative, week 9, 04/08/2026

why.say:
• PIP: coverage on the car he rode in that pays Medical Bills regardless of fault
• Harbor Point paid $685.00, $640.00, $2,395.00, then $640.00 for 03/27/2026, of $5,000; $640.00 left
• Payers in line: Harbor Point PIP, Peach State Health Plan, then a Letter of Protection
• Wrong order turns a payable bill into a lien: a debt paid from John Doe's settlement
• Red flag: at the LOP desk, a provider wants your word they'll be paid in full at settlement; you can't give it
• No amount, no reduction, no date: the LOP's terms are Atty. Thorne's

theory.say:
• After claim set-up the Case Plan has three pillars: clinical care, function, subrogation management (who gets paid back)
• Payer Order: MedPay or PIP first, health insurance second, an LOP last; the order keeps liens down
• Health insurance pays covered care at its contract rate and can claim reimbursement from the recovery
• LOP: the client's signed agreement that a provider is paid from any recovery; a lien on his take-home

theory2.say:
• Standard Treatment Map: emergency, imaging, chiropractic and therapy, orthopedics, pain management, sometimes surgery; each stop needs a payer
• Monitoring: ask about visits, gains and next week's obstacles, not just "how are you"
• Crisis intervention: step in when care is denied or stuck in paperwork; fix the immediate problem first
• Medication red flags: opioid, muscle relaxant and sedative together, or doses rising without a new diagnosis; raise with the provider

frame.say:
• Identify every payer and its default order; who is primary is Atty. Thorne's call
• MedPay or PIP: regardless of fault, to the limit; PIP also pays 80% of lost income, MedPay doesn't
• Health Plan: covered care at contract rate; may claim money back from the recovery
• LOP: last rung, for care earlier payers can't carry, paid from the recovery on Atty. Thorne's terms
• Every skipped rung is one John Doe pays for at the end

rules.say:

theory.say:
• EOB, Explanation of Benefits: the Health Plan's account of one processed claim, proof of who paid what; not a bill
• Each payer reports back: Peach State by EOB, Harbor Point by its PIP payment history; read every report before touching a lien
• RS26, Peach State's EOB: John Doe owes Crescent $0.00 for the injection
• Line by line, the proof behind demand and lien numbers: billed is the provider's charge, allowed the plan's contract amount, the in-network difference written off
• Remark codes explain each line: CO-45 is the write-off, AC1 flags a possible accident
• Member responsibility, deductible, copay, coinsurance: the most an in-network provider may bill the patient

theory2.say:
• Balance billing: billing the patient for the written-off part; in network it's an error, not a lien or debt
• PIP payment history: every check, with date of service, amount paid, limit remaining
• Exhaustion: once the limit is spent, later bills return unpaid and go to the next payer
• Reconciliation: match every provider balance to each payer's EOB or check, so no paid bill becomes a lien
• Red flag: a lien logged at the billed amount, or a bill sent to PIP after 06/26/2026; log what the plan paid

frame.say:
• Match the claim: member ID, claim number, provider, date of service against the CMS treatment record
• Billed to allowed: charge, allowed amount, write-off; then the patient's share
• What the plan paid, with date and check or electronic payment number; any payback claim starts there
• Remark codes: CO-45 explains the write-off; AC1 flags an accident and the plan's payback right
• Reconcile against the provider's statement and lien register, flag balance billing; the step most often skipped

theory.say:
• The adjuster argues the gap proves John Doe healed; a Treatment Gap is any break, read as minor, healed or unrelated
• Records made at the time by EMS, doctors and employers carry the weight, because nobody wrote them for the claim
• Examples: the 02/07/2026 Riverton Drug receipt for pain relief, notes placing pain at the collision, the EMS report, work records, later a causation opinion
• A record made to order destroys the case; the record proves continuity, not anyone's explanation of it
• Continuity of care: an unbroken path of treatment, each step following the last; adjusters test it
• Consistent histories: the same how, when and where across every chart

theory2.say:
• Causation opinion: a treating doctor linking injury to collision, the bridge across a gap; Atty. Thorne requests it
• Record integrity: changed only by the author's dated addendum; altering a record can be tampering or fraud
• Excuse notes prove only what the author saw or ordered; unexamined days need other proof
• Generic notes not tied to the collision weaken causation; flag them to Atty. Thorne, never fix them

frame.say:
• Therapy past 12 sessions with no gain and no specialist or imaging reads as stalled or over-treatment
• Passive care only, heat, TENS (electrical pulses), massage with no exercise: adjusters discount it
• Two or more missed appointments: the defense says the injury wasn't serious; the most common flag
• Surgery before therapy or injections outside an emergency; opioid, muscle relaxant and sedative together with rising doses
• Records with left and right switched, or life stress instead of the crash

rules.say:

• A record wrong at its source gets its author's dated addendum, like Summit's on 07/15/2026, and the original stays put

• Example: decision needed by 03/12/2026, approve declining Summit Imaging's LOP; the MRI goes to Harbor Point PIP
• Why: PIP applies first, $3,675.00 left; then sourced facts, then options
• If yes, send the decline and route the bill today; if no, draft the LOP for his signature
• One decision per note; log the note and his answer in the CMS the same day
rules.ask: A note holds two decisions with different deadlines. How should it be sent?

theory.say:
• Affidavit: written facts sworn under oath before a notary by someone with first-hand knowledge
• Ends in a jurat, "sworn to and subscribed before me"; a false one is perjury, which makes it proof
• Coverage: Robert Smith swears no other insurance; John, if asked, swears he lives with Margaret and owns no car
• Damages: records custodians swear bills and records are true copies; Northgate verifies wages
• Court: the process server swears Smith was served, starting his answer clock

why.say:
• A Keystone letter saying Robert Smith has no other insurance isn't enough to settle at the $10,000 limit
• Harbor Point and Cardinal State won't accept it either
• An affidavit is a word under oath from the person who knows: Smith himself, sworn 08/10/2026
• Red flag: unsigned or not notarized means it's just somebody's say-so; it goes back for signature and the jurat
• Never sign it, notarize it, or tidy up the wording yourself

rules.say:
• Smith swears no other insurance, a condition of settling at the limit
• John swears residency and no owned vehicle only if a carrier asks, from a draft Atty. Thorne reviewed
• Records requests ask for the custodian's affidavit in the same letter, so bills enter evidence without calling each provider
• Northgate's wage letter proves the $1,584.00; the affidavit of service is filed, 10/16/2026 here
• Check affiant, numbers, dates, signature, jurat and seal; defects go back; never sign, notarize or fix sworn words

steps.say:
• Demand at the limit approved: request Smith's affidavit through Keystone and docket it; sworn 08/10/2026
• Records request: include the custodian's affidavit, so the set returns ready for evidence
• Affidavit arrives: check it against the file, route any defect with a task
• File it where it'll be used: demand conditions, UM packages, the trial binder
steps.ask: An affidavit arrives signed but with no notary seal. What happens, and who is told?

case.say:
• 04/24/2026, 3:30 p.m.: John is back in care; two months of treatment paper filed in the CMS
• Urgent Care first-visit note, Spine and Rehab evaluation with the LOP, Lakeside consult, Summit Imaging MRI invoice
• A colleague's backup put the Summit invoice in 03 Medical Records
• July's pre-demand audit totals bills from the bills folder, so the $2,395.00 would be missed

task.say:
• File the four documents in the CMS from Work From, so each copy lands in its backup folder
• Notes, evaluations, consults go to 03 Medical Records; invoices to 04 Bills & Invoices
• In Google Drive, move, not copy, the Summit invoice into 04 Bills & Invoices, and rename it by the naming convention on the slide
• Open My Backup Drive and run Check my drive
• Write the records-versus-bills rule in two sentences in Case Notes

check.say:
• Urgent Care note, evaluation and Lakeside consult in 03 Medical Records
• Summit invoice in 04 Bills & Invoices, once only
• Dashboard backed-up count matches what was filed; Check my drive shows nothing missing
• Records say what was done to John; bills say what it cost; kept apart, the Specials add up
check.ask: A bill turns up in the records folder the week before the demand. What else gets checked?
